summary: the text-literal escape `\0` decodes to a zero byte
instruction: Change request for the A0 front end (lexer and parser): in a `text "..."` literal the escape `\0` (a backslash, then the digit zero) must decode to the byte 0. A zero digit that is not escaped is still the byte 48, and the other escapes are unchanged.

tests.src:
fn f -> u32
t text "0\00\n"
ret 0
end

fn f -> u32
t text "\\0\0"
ret 0
end

fn sq u32 -> u32
a mul p0 p0
ret a
end

# a small program
use "lib.a0"
fn inc u32 -> u32
a add p0 1 # one more
ret a
end
fn g u32x4 (u32,bool) -> u32
b at p1 0
c get p0 2
d call inc c
e div d 3
f select true e b
t text "hi\n"
ret f
end

fn h u32x4x2 boolx3 -> (u32,u32x4)
x get p0 1
y get x 0
z rec y x
ret z
end
fn k u32 u32 -> u32
ret sub p0 p1
end

reference.a0:
isz eq c 48 @ ist
m2 select isz 0 m1 @ m1
v select e1 m2 c

wrong.a0:
isz eq c 48 @ ist
m2 select isz 0 m1 @ m1
w0 select isz 0 c @ m2
v select e1 m2 w0
wrong.why: A0: the zero is decoded whether or not it was escaped; TS: the mapping is written the wrong way round (byte 0 to 48)
